incidents.name: ParaSwap Augustus V6 arbitrary-call approval drain
incidents.notes: AugustusV6.uniswapV3SwapCallback() did not verify that msg.sender was a genuine Uniswap V3 pool and trusted the caller-supplied data for the payer and token, so anyone could invoke it directly and make the router transferFrom any wallet that had approved it.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x00000000fdac7708d0d360bddc1bc7d097f47439 is the verified AugustusV6 contract created 2024-03-13 by 0x91cee75acbdd7be57bacb40fdeaa4e27dc5154b3 (ParaSwap deployer), not by the extractor 0xfde0d1575ed8e06fbf36256bcdfa1f359281455a; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events between creation and the incident block Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): AugustusV6 is a diamond: its fallback DELEGATECALLs a facet looked up in diamond storage, so the executing code can change without an EIP-1967 event. Exactly two DiamondCut(...) logs (topic 0x8faa70878671ccd212d20771b795c50af8fd3ff6cf27f4bde57e5d4de0aeb673) exist between the creation block 19426044 and the incident block 19470561: the first inside the creation tx 0xc2106bf2138a03abfca84ae3cd5465fc64ad29caed5d27b7523059517572a0ef (facet 0x45961104C01199eaa552046290ad3B12513600cB), the second in tx 0xb18ac879242944544f397d3f20d511085b507cf45bdbd5cd2cf52c57076df5f5 at block 19426051, 2024-03-13T12:07:59Z (timestamp 1710331679), 84 seconds later, adding four more facets plus an init contract 0xfc6dd98f962bb487289c8ad4f3a2732972a1ad34 - a ParaSwap deployer action, not the attacker's. Measuring from that last cut gives codeAgeSeconds 1710872735-1710331679 = 541056 instead of 541140, an 84-second correction. The exploited entry point itself did not move: facetAddress(0xfa461e33) for uniswapV3SwapCallback(int256,int256,bytes) returns the zero address at the incident block, i.e. the callback is served by the diamond's own runtime, which is byte-identical at the creation and incident blocks, and facetAddresses() returns the same five facets from the second cut through the incident.

incidents.name: ParaSwap Augustus V5 simpleSwap arbitrary-callee approval drain
incidents.notes: AugustusSwapper.simpleSwap() executes caller-supplied callee/exchangeData sequences as the router itself, so an attacker who flash-borrowed 1000 wei of WETH as the nominal fromToken could have the router run DAI.move against an account that still held a ParaSwap authorisation and forward the proceeds to an attacker-chosen beneficiary.

sources.ref: onchain review: AugustusSwapper V5 0xdef171fe48cf0115b1d80b88dc8eab59176fee57 created 2021-08-18T12:42:05Z by 0xf01121e808f782d7f34e857c27da31ad1f151b39, not the attack-tx sender 0x2d9a39de3e5227ff74b4cfc154b16fd77614ee33; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the Augustus address itself, 1406.6 days old. Same arbitrary-callee family as the recorded Augustus V6 row but a different deployment and a different transaction. 2,299.04 DAI drained from 0x1e0c22a1f39b6c7f36661297437e874ec31fa0b1, taken at 1:1 as a USD-pegged stable.

delegatecall-target review (callTracer + prestateTracer on the exploit tx, then eth_getStorageAt over [creation block, incident block]): AugustusSwapper V5 is a per-selector route table, not a single-implementation proxy. The exploit tx makes exactly one DELEGATECALL, 0xdef171fe...ee57 -> 0x66c1c25d7d2bd4a32ed33501e202b275030f402c with selector 0x54e3f31b (simpleSwap), and prestateTracer shows that address read from mapping slot 0xd0d6677800a993d9f57d5429a1a7401f674e568d0f74ca8057f1e2e320362e92. Binary-searching that slot between the creation block 13049291 and the incident block 22778355 gives seven writes: 0x7a5a0be8 (2021-08-18T13:30:43Z), 0xba7fe1aa (2021-08-18T13:59:08Z), cleared to zero (2022-01-06), 0x2938bc86 (2022-01-10), 0xa655d026 (2022-02-24), 0x6e8b66cc (2022-06-15) and 0x66c1c25d7d2bd4a32ed33501e202b275030f402c at block 17472047, 2023-06-13T15:45:23Z, constant across 60 samples up to the incident. The exploited simpleSwap code was therefore 742.4 days old, not the 1406.6 days measured from the Augustus deployment
